Thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap + next steps from our demo focused on logging controls and sensitive-data redaction:

Key asks you mentioned:
- Don’t persist PII in request/response logs (PII includes: full names, SSNs, bank account numbers, API keys, JWTs).
- Ability to redact or mask headers (e.g., Authorization, Cookie, x-correlation-id) and to obfuscate trace IDs so they’re not reversible.
- Configurable retention window for logs (target: 90 days, with option for shorter retention).
- Ability to disable request/response body logging entirely for specific routes/environments.
- Examples of redacted vs raw logs so Legal/security can validate.
- SOC2/pen-test evidence and KMS/HSM integration for keys.

Attachments: I’ve attached a draft "redaction-controls-v1.pdf" that summarizes our supported controls and the SOW draft you requested (SOW-draft-FinTechCo.docx).

2) Provide a couple of redacted log examples and a short runbook describing how we configure route-level logging policies.
3) Schedule a 30-45m security deep-dive with your InfoSec / Legal (we can include our compliance lead).

Can you confirm the retention target (90 days) or let us know if you need 30/60/365? Also confirm whether disabling request/response logs entirely for certain production routes is an absolute requirement or a preference.

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the details, this is helpful. Below are the concrete options Redwood supports and the tradeoffs so your team can pick what meets your security posture.

Summary of options (short):
- Trace ID handling:
  - One-way salted hashing at ingress: we can hash trace IDs on receipt using a customer-specific salt (stored in your KMS) so only the hash persists. This prevents reversal and still lets you correlate events by hashed ID.
  - Replace with internal UUID: drop the incoming value and attach a server-generated UUID; original trace is never persisted.
- Header scrubbing:
  - Route-level header allowlist/denylist with regex redaction rules. We support both name-based header removal (drop header entirely) and value redaction (masking, regex replace).
- Request/response redaction:
  - PII classifier + scrubber pipeline: tokens matching PII patterns (SSN, email, card numbers) are replaced with TTL-labeled placeholders (e.g., <REDACTED_EMAIL>).
  - Field-level redaction via OpenAPI schema or JSONPath for structured payloads (we can strip specific JSON paths on route).
- Sampling / retention:
  - Sampling: per-route sample rate (0.01% - 100%). Sampled logs are stored exactly like full logs but you control rate.
  - Retention: configurable at tenant/route level (30 / 90 / 365 days). Shortening retention reduces storage and cost.
- Disable logging:
  - Route-level flag to disable storing request/response bodies entirely; metadata (status codes, duration, non-sensitive headers) can still be recorded for metrics and SLOs.
- Encryption & audit:
  - Logs encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys (KMS). Audit trails for any access to logs, with roles/SCIM integration.

Cost / overhead notes:
- Enabling full request/response logging increases storage and egress for support/debugging — typical cost delta ~2-4x compared to metadata-only, depending on payload sizes and sampling rate.
- Sampling reduces cost linearly with the sample rate. Example: 0.1% sampling yields ~1/1000th of storage for body data.

Example redaction output (sanitized):
--- raw request ---
{
  "user_name": "Priya Rao",
  "ssn": "123-45-6789",
  "account": "XXXXX-6789",
  "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1..."
}
--- redacted (PII classifier + field rules) ---
{
  "user_name": "<REDACTED_NAME>",
  "ssn": "<REDACTED_SSN>",
  "account": "<REDACTED_ACCOUNT>",
  "token": "<REDACTED_TOKEN>"
}

Header example: Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>
x-ft-user-id: <REDACTED_ID>
